purpose: Derive the finite-community to Gaussian/diffusion to deterministic mean-field ladder for the zero-trait-adjustment Chapter 2 submodel without changing the empirical claim ceiling.

model_scope.mark_distribution: unchanged make_pollinator distribution; survival is mark-independent
model_scope.response_coordinate: terminal community interaction-kernel contrast K_island(x)-K_mainland(x); service has the same sign because saturation is monotone

exact_count_layer.method: propagate the full terminal count pmf by binomial thinning plus Bernoulli immigration
exact_count_layer.expected_scaling_test: for k independent pooled copies, count CV must equal the k=1 CV divided by sqrt(k) up to floating-point tolerance

kernel_moment_layer.mark_moments: deterministic quadrature over the clamped-normal pollinator trait distribution and the frozen generalist/specialist/introduced mixtures

gaussian_layer.approximation: multivariate Gaussian with the exact finite-k kernel-contrast mean and covariance
gaussian_layer.probability_evaluation: fixed-seed Gaussian Monte Carlo over the 21-dimensional trait grid

comparison_to_abm.metric: pooled mixed-realization fraction across the six prespecified seeds

decision_rules.mean_field_geometry: classify the sign of the deterministic kernel contrast on all 21 trait-grid points without retuning
decision_rules.gaussian_accuracy: report absolute mixed-probability error versus the pooled ABM estimate at k=1,2,4,8,16; no post-hoc threshold selection
decision_rules.asymptotic_branching: if the mean-field contrast has one sign at every grid point, finite-community mixed branching must vanish asymptotically; if the mean-field contrast is mixed, branching survives the deterministic limit

prohibited: calling the Gaussian approximation an exact Fokker-Planck solution
calling k=1024 the exact mean-field limit
using a result-dependent k grid or RNG seed
interpreting pooled-copy k as a natural pollinator abundance estimate
changing the three-result empirical narrative or the historical 0/25 claim boundary
claim_boundary: This is a theory/approximation audit of the frozen zero-trait-adjustment synthetic submodel. It may clarify whether finite-community branching converges to a deterministic mean-field response, but it is not an empirical abundance model, an LNA validation for the full adaptive model, or a replacement for the finite-community simulation used in Chapter 2.
